Both of these proteins are targets of different compounds, with the latter being targeted by (-)-Sophoramine, which in turn targets ATR. The scores for these relationships indicate varying levels of confidence, with the first pathway having a slightly higher score. This suggests that Cholesteryl chloride may interact with ATR through different molecular mechanisms, possibly through the modulation of intermediate proteins. The evidence highlights the complexity of the relationship, emphasizing the need for further investigation into the specific mechanisms by which Cholesteryl chloride influences ATR activity.
